title: My Husband Told Me Our Daughter’s Wedding Was Canceled — Then I Saw Photos Of Him Walking Another Woman Down The Aisle In Her Place (PART 2) – Story Loom

blocks.text: …your husband. He told the venue our daughter had been hospitalized and had given him power of attorney to transfer the booking.”

The young woman in my daughter’s dress was named Chloe. She was twenty-six. My husband, Paul, was her father. He had another family two hours away, a second wife who believed I’d died before Chloe was born.

Chloe’s own wedding plans had fallen through when the venue she wanted was fully booked. Paul saw a chance. He told our daughter, Emma, that I’d lost all our savings and that the wedding had to be postponed. He told me Emma had called it off and didn’t want to talk. Then he transferred the booking, the flowers and even the dress, which was waiting at the boutique, to Chloe.
Emma had been heartbroken too. Paul had told her I was “too upset to talk.” Neither of us called each other because each of us thought the other needed space.
Chloe took off the veil right there in the venue. She was shaking. “I didn’t know,” she said, again and again. “I swear I didn’t know about you.”
Paul was charged with fraud and bigamy. His second wife filed for an annulment within the month. My attorney recovered the $28,000 I’d paid, since the venue had been booked under my name and my card.

Emma married her fiancé three months later, in the same venue, in a new dress she chose herself. I walked her down the aisle. Chloe came too, at Emma’s invitation. She sat in the back and cried through the vows.

Afterward, Chloe found me by the cake and said, “I’m sorry I wore her dress.” I told her none of this was her fault. She’s my daughter’s half-sister. They have lunch once a month now. They both have Paul’s eyes, and neither of them has his heart. That’s the best thing I can say about him.
